top_signals.title: Bessent ‘Economic D-Day’ Seen as Warning Shot
top_signals.summary:
The US “economic D-Day” against Iran turned out to be less Normandy and more Grenada, with Scott Bessent providing few details on how the administration’s new initiative would achieve any of Donald Trump’s desired results, namely the full opening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Dan Tannebaum, Global Anti-Financial Crime Practice Leader at Oliver Wyman, discusses the move from Bessent and how previous threats from the Trump Administration, particularly in the tariff space, compare. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: The Netherlands to Miss Natural Gas Filling Target for Winter
top_signals.summary: The Netherlands will miss its target to fill natural gas storage sites ahead of the winter, its gas network operators said on Wednesday, in one of the first evidence-based signs that Europe may be struggling to have sufficient supply for a harsh winter. Gasunie, the Dutch gas network operator, on Wednesday warned that the country will miss its target to have 115 terawatt-hours (TWh) worth of gas supply. top_signals.title: UK Government Takes Stake in Tungsten Mine With £71m Mine Bet
top_signals.summary: The government’s National Wealth Fund is set to pump £71m into miner Tungsten West in a bid to help reopen the Hemerdon mine in Devon. The funding package combines a £36m share purchase, which will hand the government a 7.4 per cent stake in Tungsten and a seat on the board of directors, and a £25m loan facility. The project is expected to boost the local economy in the South West of England through the creation of 350 direct jobs.
